All 4 Nov 2026 5 Nov 2026 6 Nov 2026 In-Person PDT Online UTC Filters In-Person PDT Online UTC Filters Wed 4 Nov Wed 4 Nov 6:00 pm In-Person only Registration required San Francisco Walking Tour 🌉 6:00 pm In-Person only Registration required San Francisco Walking Tour 🌉 Wed 4 Nov 6:00 pm In-Person only Registration required San Francisco Walking Tour 🌉 1h 30m 6:00 pm 7:30 pm Thu 5 Nov Thu 5 Nov 8:30 am In-Person only Registration Open + Coffee Thu 5 Nov 9:00 am In-Person only Opening Remarks from Our Host Jim Morris opens UXDX San Francisco and sets the scene for the day ahead. He'll connect the themes running across the programme, from how AI is changing individual product roles to how teams build, make decisions and organize around the work. Throughout the day, Jim will guide us between sessions, pull out the connections and help turn individual talks into one broader conversation about what AI-native product development actually looks like in practice. Jim Morris Founder Flywheel Product Group Thu 5 Nov 9:15 am Is AI Killing Design? The story is everywhere: AI is coming for design. Wireframes, mockups, prototypes, specs — produced by a model in seconds. The panic is loud, and most of it is aimed at the wrong half of the work. In this keynote, Richard makes a more uncomfortable case: AI isn't the threat designers think it is — it's exposing a different problem they should have been worried about all along. Attendees will learn how to: Spot the part of design work that's about to disappear, and the part about to define the next decade. Identify the documents that turn generic AI output into work that reflects real users, real businesses, and real context. Rethink design roles, titles, and team structure for a world where production is no longer the job. Richard Dalton Chief Design Officer Thu 5 Nov 9:50 am Who Controls the Customer Journey in Agentic AI? As AI systems become more capable, products are increasingly able to act on behalf of users, recommending, planning, personalizing, purchasing, and completing tasks with minimal intervention. While these experiences can dramatically reduce effort, they also introduce new challenges around trust, transparency, consent, and control. The most successful AI-powered products are not those that automate the most. They are the ones that help users feel confident, informed, and in control as automation increases. Moderated by Alex Burke, CEO of Optimal, this session will explore how leading consumer product organizations are designing agentic experiences that deliver convenience without sacrificing user agency. Determining which actions should be automated and which require explicit user approval based on risk, context, and customer expectations. Designing transparency, consent, and intervention mechanisms that help users understand, monitor, and influence AI-driven decisions. Building trust in products that interpret intent, handle personal data, and take action on behalf of users in real-world scenarios. Creating agentic experiences that reduce friction while maintaining user confidence, accountability, and control. Alex Burke CEO Optimal Rachel Been SVP of Design Expedia Group Purvi Shah SVP, Head of User Experience Design, Research, and Accessibility Target Chris Stang Chief Product Officer for Digital Chase Thu 5 Nov 10:35 am When Your Customer Is an AI: Building Ad Platforms for the Age of Autonomous Marketing As AI agents increasingly create campaigns, generate creative assets, allocate budgets, optimize performance, and analyze results, advertising platforms are undergoing a fundamental shift. The primary user is no longer just the marketer. Increasingly, it is the AI acting on their behalf. Drawing on her experience leading Ads Platform at Snap, Shobha Diwakar explores how product teams can design platforms that effectively serve both human and AI users while maintaining trust, transparency, and control. In this session, Shobha will explore: Designing advertising platforms for AI-driven decision making, including how campaign creation, targeting, bidding, optimization, and measurement evolve when AI becomes a primary user of the system. Defining the boundaries between human judgment and AI autonomy, balancing automation with the oversight, control, and accountability marketers expect. Building trust in AI-powered products, using transparency, explainability, and feedback mechanisms that increase adoption while maintaining confidence in automated outcomes. Through practical examples and lessons from building advertising technology at scale, this session will provide product, design, and engineering leaders with a framework for creating products where AI is increasingly both the user and the decision-maker. Shobha Diwakar VP, Ads Product & Engineering Snap Inc. Thu 5 Nov 11:10 am Networking Break Thu 5 Nov 11:35 am The Intent Steward Model: How Sephora is Redesigning Product Delivery for AI-Native Teams What had to change inside Sephora when customer journeys became fluid, with customers entering through search, social, AI assistants and other unpredictable entry points. How Sephora's Intent Steward model helps teams design systems that understand customer intent, apply context and determine the next best action in real time. The operating model, guardrails and cross-functional collaboration required to build and govern AI-powered decisioning systems. A detailed case study showing how Sephora applied these principles to a real customer or partner experience, and how the team's role shifted from shipping features to orchestrating outcomes. Sneha Narahalli SVP, Head of Product & UX Sephora Thu 5 Nov 12:10 pm Beyond the Pilot: Scaling AI from Experimentation to Business Impact Most organizations have launched AI experiments. Far fewer have successfully scaled them into products, workflows, and operating models that deliver measurable customer and business value. Moving from isolated pilots to organization-wide adoption requires new approaches to governance, measurement, risk management, and prioritization. This session explores what separates successful AI transformations from costly experimentation. Prioritizing AI initiatives based on customer value, business outcomes, and implementation effort. Establishing governance frameworks that balance innovation, compliance, and risk. Measuring the impact of AI initiatives beyond usage metrics and experimentation. Scaling successful AI capabilities across teams, products, and customer experiences. Maz Brumand VP of Product ŌURA Thu 5 Nov 12:45 pm Lunch and Networking Break 🥗 Thu 5 Nov 1:45 pm AI Is Blurring Product Roles. Now What? AI tools are reshaping how product, design and engineering work together, where responsibilities sit, and what it means to contribute to product development. In this session, Ashley Nutter shares how CNN is thinking about AI adoption across product teams, from encouraging experimentation to avoiding tool proliferation, spreading useful practices, and deciding when workflows should be standardised. This talk looks at the operating model questions leaders now need to answer: how teams collaborate, how roles evolve, and how organizations keep momentum without creating chaos. Ashley will share practical lessons from a large media organization navigating AI transformation, with a focus on the people, process and leadership decisions that make adoption sustainable. Ashley Nutter SVP, Product & Design CNN Thu 5 Nov 2:20 pm How Do You Evolve a Product Billions of People Trust? Google Search is undergoing one of the most consequential transformations in its history as AI changes how people find, understand and act on information. In this fireside, Rhi Bell shares the real decisions behind evolving a product used by billions: what changes, what must remain familiar, and how the team balances speed and creative possibility with trust, user agency and judgment. The conversation will explore the tradeoffs, challenges and lessons from designing new AI-powered Search experiences, not just the finished vision. Rhiannon “Rhi” Bell Vice President of User Experience, Google Search Google Thu 5 Nov 2:55 pm Networking Break Thu 5 Nov 3:20 pm When Everyone Can Build, What Happens to Product Teams? AI is enabling designers, engineers and product managers to move from an idea to a polished prototype or working product faster than ever. But when almost anyone can build, speed is no longer the main constraint. The bigger risk is building the wrong thing faster. Josh Clemm, Vice President of Software Engineering at Figma, and David Hoang, Head of Design at Atlassian, explore what this shift means for product teams: How teams can use AI to expand who contributes without losing direction and clarity. When to add friction and deliberate decision-making rather than optimizing for output alone. How product, design and engineering roles, ownership and collaboration need to evolve. Why judgment, taste, design thinking and technical quality become more valuable as building gets easier. David Hoang VP of Design - Rovo & AI, Ecosystem, and DevAI Atlassian Josh Clemm Vice President, Software Engineering Figma Thu 5 Nov 3:55 pm Building Products in the Age of AI: Inside Uber’s Software Factory AI is changing how teams at Uber build products, reshaping every step from the first idea to what customers experience. In this session, we'll share how Uber built its Software Factory: a lifecycle-wide system of agents, infrastructure, and workflows that spans Plan → Build → Validate → Deploy → Observe → Maintain, and what we're learning as these new ways of working evolve at scale. We'll walk through how work moves through the lifecycle today, where agents take on tasks that once required a handoff between product, design, and engineering, and how that is compressing the loop between understanding a problem, shaping an idea, prototyping it, shipping it, and learning from customers. A growing share of that work is no longer initiated by a person at all: managed agents review code, heal failing builds, complete end-to-end changes with visual validation, triage alerts, and handle maintenance, with humans reviewing and escalating. Today, more than 70% of Uber's pull requests originate from local or cloud agents, and teams have built thousands of reusable agent skills across the lifecycle. We'll also look at the technology behind this shift, including how we enable agents to securely understand Uber's systems through a company-wide context graph, gateways for models and tools, and cloud development environments, and how we measure whether each agent is delivering value, not just output. Along the way, we'll share what changed, the challenges we hit, and where human creativity, context, and judgment remain essential. Uday Kiran Medisetty VP, Distinguished Engineer Uber Sumanth Sukumar VP, Engineering Uber Thu 5 Nov 4:30 pm The Next Interface Is the Organization AI isn’t just changing what teams build. It’s redesigning work itself. As roles and workflows shift, product, design and engineering leaders must move beyond products and services to shape how the organization works. Even the strongest AI vision will fail if the organization cannot absorb it. This session explores how to design organizations that are ready to turn AI’s potential into real change: How do we redesign jobs and workflows around AI? What can design bring to organizational transformation? Why do traditional change programs fail to change how work actually happens? How can employees help shape the AI-driven organization they’ll work within? Jod Kaftan Digital Experience Design Senior Director NTT DATA Cynthia Kaschub Senior Director, Workforce Innovation Salesforce Payal Fofadiya Engineering Manager, Agent Platform LinkedIn Shipra Kayan Chief Design Evangelist Miro Thu 5 Nov 5:10 pm In-Person only Closing Remarks by Our Host Jim brings the day together, reflecting on the biggest ideas, tensions and practical lessons from across the programme before we continue the conversation over drinks. AI can now generate discussion guides, summarize interviews, identify patterns, and produce research reports in minutes. But not every part of the research process should be automated. The most successful teams understand where AI adds value, where human judgment remains essential, and how to combine both effectively. This workshop explores how AI is reshaping user research and provides practical frameworks for deciding what to automate, what to augment, and what should remain human-led. In this workshop, you'll learn how to: Evaluate which research activities can be effectively automated and where human researchers continue to provide unique value. Use AI to accelerate analysis, synthesis, and insight generation without compromising research quality or rigor. Design research workflows that combine AI efficiency with human judgment to improve speed and decision-making. Avoid common risks and biases in AI-assisted research while maintaining confidence in customer insights and recommendations. Ideal for: UX Researchers, Designers, Research & Design Leads, Research Operations, and UX Managers within enterprise organisations who are already using AI in parts of their workflow and want practical guidance on applying it more effectively. Registration required Gabe Young Head of Product Innovation Optimal Josh Walker Senior Product Designer Optimal In-Person only AI-Powered Product Discovery: Finding Opportunities Faster and Validating Ideas at Scale "AI is transforming how teams discover customer needs, identify opportunities, and validate ideas. The challenge is no longer accessing customer feedback. It's knowing how to combine AI-powered analysis with customer conversations, research, and human judgment to make better product decisions faster. In this hands-on workshop, you'll explore how leading product teams are integrating AI into their discovery process while avoiding the common pitfalls of over-relying on automated insights. In this workshop, you'll learn how to: Identify customer problems and emerging opportunities faster by combining AI-powered analysis with continuous customer discovery. Accelerate opportunity validation using AI-assisted research, synthesis, and feedback analysis techniques. Prioritize customer needs with greater confidence by balancing AI-generated insights with qualitative research and business context. Build scalable discovery workflows that help product teams stay connected to customers without slowing down delivery." Registration required Shipra Kayan Chief Design Evangelist Miro Fri 6 Nov 1:15 pm In-Person only How to Measure AI-Powered Experiences Teams are rapidly introducing AI features but there is still no established way to measure whether those experiences are accurate, understandable and worthy of users’ trust. Traditional UX metrics alone may not capture what happens when outputs are generated by AI and can change from one interaction to the next.
